populationDefinition: Selected public records sufficient to test the proposed WOW List-popular.vote-Call Script-NYC Artist Coalition formation lineage; not a complete archive of every formation conversation, host, or participant.

sequence.finding: The shared project account routed people to popular.vote for marches, meetings, and local connection.
sequence.boundary: The record does not assign individual post authorship or prove popular.vote use or impact.

sequence.finding: The surviving public Page links directly to popular.vote and routes to NYC Artist Coalition meetings.
sequence.boundary: The current Page does not prove individual authorship, complete history, audience, or impact.

sequence.surface: NYC DIY Spaces post Ghost Ship: Dept of Cultural Affairs Meeting
sequence.finding: The public event identifies NYC Artist Coalition and Call Script among its displayed hosts and shows 445 people responded.
sequence.boundary: The response signal is not attendance, unique people, endorsement, or a complete host record.

sequence.finding: Institutional discussion posts used a date poll to invite a follow-up meeting, linked the February 6 coalition general meeting, and invited people to help choose the work.
sequence.boundary: The institutional discussion sequence does not establish Jamie's authorship of every post or the complete formation history.

sequence.surface: DIY: NYC Artist Coalition - General Meeting
sequence.finding: The linked follow-up became a named coalition general meeting at Magick City with collective priority-setting language.
sequence.boundary: The meeting record does not establish the complete founding group, physical attendance, or sole causality.

jamieRoleBoundary.supported: Jamie confirms establishing Call Script and carrying participation-system lessons from WOW List and popular.vote into early coalition convening; the public sequence corroborates the project and event lineage.
